Seen on 2026-09-04: the child died with "Remove the credential and run: claude auth login".

Not reproducible from this session. Every path was tested and all of them worked: the inherited environment, a scrubbed environment with only HOME, PATH, USER and SHELL, and all three claude binaries on PATH — .local/bin, homebrew, and Conductor's pinned 2.1.257.

So the difference is the shell that started `werk serve`. OAuth lives in the login Keychain under the service "Claude Code-credentials", and Keychain access is granted per application. A terminal that has not been granted access, or a stale credential, fails exactly this way.

src/agent.ts owns one long-lived claude child. The server exposes POST /api/chat and streams every message back over the existing SSE channel.

Three things that make it work.

1. The open card is prepended only when it changes, as a compact block built from the map itself: title, why, kind, status, who, children and depends_on. Navigating without typing sends nothing.
2. The agent's allowlist is 'Bash(node src/cli.ts:*)' plus read-only tools. It maintains the map and cannot edit code. Widen with 'serve --allow'.
3. When the agent runs a werk command, log.jsonl changes, fs.watch fires, and every open map reloads. The transcript in .werk/chat.jsonl never triggers a redraw.

card werk-context-pie  [decided]
A context-fill pie next to the model selector, with a clear-context popover
why: Token usage was invisible until the child crashed or slowed down near the window limit.

The pie reads modelUsage from the CLI's own 'result' event — inputTokens + outputTokens + cacheReadInputTokens + cacheCreationInputTokens over contextWindow, both reported by the model itself, so the fill and the limit are never a guess baked into this file. It turns var(--proto) blue under 33%, var(--open) yellow from 33%, var(--stale) red from 66%, drawn with a conic-gradient on a 16px button — no canvas, no chart library.

Clicking it opens a popover with the percentage and a Clear context button. Agent.clearContext() drops the stored session id and the chat.jsonl transcript, then restarts the child the same way setModel does: kill, flagged as deliberate so the exit handler skips the crash-reporting path, restart. The map itself is untouched — only the chat forgets. Same busy guard as switching models: --model and a cleared context both only take effect at spawn, so the pane refuses both mid-turn.

  -> refines         werk-model-select  A model selector in the chat header: Sonnet, Opus, Sonnet + Opus advisor
  <- depends_on      werk-head-bottom  The chat header sits below the composer, not above the log

card werk-mc-fork  [decided]
Fork the session, do not start it empty
why: Claude Code supports --fork-session. A fork keeps the shared prefix, so the cache still hits.

Confirmed. `--fork-session` hits the cache in full, and the parent is untouched.

## Method

`cd /tmp/werk-fork-proto` (scratch, outside this repo). Three `claude --print --output-format json` calls, same model:

1. A baseline turn carrying ~70k tokens of filler, no history.
2. A plain `--resume <session>` turn: a two-word reply, no new content.
3. A `--resume <session> --fork-session` turn: same, but forked.

## Result

    call        cache_creation_input_tokens   cache_read_input_tokens
    baseline    70118                         0
    control     61                            70118
    fork        61                            70179

The fork's `cache_read_input_tokens` (70179) equals the full prefix at the moment of the fork — the baseline plus the control turn, both already written to cache. It pays cache-read price for all of it and only writes 61 new tokens, the same number the plain control turn wrote for its own new content. A fresh, empty context would have paid full input price for that turn's own text and nothing else — cheaper in isolation, but it would then re-read every file and every card body the parent conversation already holds, on its own turns.

## What actually happens on disk

    ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/f35a3cc8-....jsonl   parent: baseline, control. Stops there.
    ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/29559e9c-....jsonl   fork: baseline, control, then its own FORK turn.

The fork is a full copy of the parent's history up to the fork point, under its own session id, as its own file. The parent file gains no fork turn — confirmed by reading both files after the run. So `resolveConvo` in src/convos.ts, which already keys off a session id, needs no change for this: a fork is just another session id with its own `chat.jsonl`.

## What this settles

- Werk's fork button should call `claude --resume <parent-session> --fork-session`, not start empty by default. #werk-mc-fork:opt0 stays the explicit second choice.
- The fold point for #werk-mc-shared's 'what changed since' question is exactly this: the last event each side saw as of the fork's parent-session read, which the log's `seq` numbers already carry.
- No further prototype needed here. The remaining unknown was fidelity of the cache hit under `--fork-session` specifically (as opposed to a bare new session), and it hit in full.

Both fixed in `src/agent.ts` and `src/convo-manager.ts`, recorded on **#werk-context-pie-fork**.

1. `ConvoManager.fork()` now passes the parent's live `context()` into the new Agent, so the pie shows the inherited size immediately instead of 0% until the first turn.
2. `clearContext()` now also clears `forkFrom`, so clicking Clear before the first message actually starts the next turn empty instead of silently re-forking the parent.
